topIssues.title: op-supernode: superroot_atTimestamp optimistic RequiredL1 reports cross-safe L1, not local-safe L1
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
`OptimisticAtTimestamp[chain].RequiredL1` in `superroot_atTimestamp` reports the L1 at which `chain`'s at-T block was cross-safe-promoted, not the L1 at which it became local-safe. The optimistic branch needs the local-safe L1 — that's the L1 a fault-prover deriving optimistically needs to see.

`OptimisticAt` (`op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/chain_container.go:508`) → `safeDBAtL2` → `virtual_node.L1AtSafeHead` walks op-node's safeDB. That safeDB is only written by `SafeHeadUpdated` (`op-node/node/safedb/safedb.go:101`), invoked from `SafeDerivedEvent` → `PromoteSafe` → `IndexingMode.UpdateCrossSafe(derived, derivedFrom)` — i.e. the cross-safe promotion path. The local-safe L1 is never recorded. Any optimistic block whose cross-validation must wait on another chain has `RequiredL1` arbitrarily later than its local-safe L1; op-challenger's `provider_supernode.go:126` then short-circuits to `InvalidTransition` for L1 heads at which kona produces the proper transition.

Reproduction: #20662 (two acceptance tests, with and without an eventual replacement; both fail identically).

## Fix shape

Surface the local-safe-derived L1 from `LocalSafeUpdateEvent` into the per-chain virtual node and have `OptimisticAt` consult it instead of the cross-safe-keyed safeDB.

## Note

The original framing of this issue blamed deny-list pairing (`safeDBAtL2(replacement.ID())` vs the original block's L1). That was wrong — the no-replacement variant in #20662 exhibits the same mismatch, so the cause is the safeDB itself, not the replacement path.

---
**Claude:** Filed by Claude on behalf of @AdrianSutton.

topIssues.title: Kona frame parsing mismatch against op-node and OP Stack Specs
topIssues.author: kevin-valerio
topIssues.body:
## Bug description

The [OP Stack derivation spec defines](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/derivation.html#:~:text=is_last%20is%20a%20single%20byte%20with%20a%20value%20of%201%20if%20the%20frame%20is%20the%20last%20in%20the%20channel%2C%200%20if%20there%20are%20frames%20in%20the%20channel.%20Any%20other%20value%20makes%20the%20frame%20invalid%20(it%20must%20be%20ignored%20by%20the%20rollup%20node).) `is_last` as a byte that must be 0 or 1 and any other value makes the frame invalid and it must be ignored by the rollup node. The same spec [also](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/derivation.html#:~:text=All%20frames%20in%20a%20batcher%20transaction%20must%20be%20parseable.%20If%20any%20one%20frame%20fails%20to%20parse%2C%20the%20all%20frames%20in%20the%20transaction%20are%20rejected.) states that all frames in a batcher transaction must be parseable, and if any frame fails to parse, then all frames in that transaction are rejected.

However, the `kona-protocol` frame decoder accepts invalid `is_last` bytes, while `op-node` rejects them. This parsing mismatch can make the Rust pipeline accept L1 batch inbox data that op-node rejects. If a system uses both implementations (for example a node in Go and a proof program in Rust), it can cause client disagreement and different L2 inputs.

On the Go side, op-node implements properly the spec: Frame.UnmarshalBinary returns an error for any `is_last` other than 0 or 1. However, on the Rust side (Kona), `Frame::decode` currently treats `is_last` as (byte == 1), meaning invalid values like 2 are accepted as false instead of being rejected.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2eb7e3c074b6b77cf94956529508ec882b0b5f18/op-node/rollup/derive/frame.go#L105-L107

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2eb7e3c074b6b77cf94956529508ec882b0b5f18/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/frame.rs#L210-L212

## Impact Details
If a Kona-based proof path is used to judge claims (CANNON_KONA as the used game type), it can validate an output root claim that does not match the spec and op-node which can cause an incorrect dispute outcome. Noting that with [upgrade 18](https://docs.optimism.io/notices/upgrade-18) which adds CANNON_KONA (8) with CANNON (0) to add Kona's fault proof path to run with the Go path, chains can have CANNON_KONA (8) becomes the respected game type, making this bug production ready.

## Risk

A serialization bug in the batcher service writes is_last = 2 for frame 0 of a channel, while the rest of the frame fields are correct. The batcher posts two L1 transactions to the batch inbox: the first contains frame 0 with is_last = 2 (instead of 0), and the second contains frame 1 with is_last = 1. A Go op-node rejects the first transaction during frame parsing (invalid is_last), and per spec the transaction’s frames are rejected, so it cannot assemble the channel from the second transaction alone.

A Rust kona pipeline accepts the first transaction, treats is_last = 2 as false, and assembles a complete channel after ingesting the second transaction. If the channel bytes decompress and decode into batches, the Rust fault proof program derives an output root that differs from the spec/Go output root for the same L1 head, and the system can reach a state where the fault proof program and op-node disagree on whether an output root claim is valid.

## Fix
The fix is straight-forward, validate that is_last is either 0 or 1 during frame decoding, and reject any other value, so it matches the spec and op-node.

## Author notes
This bug was initially reported in Immunefi but closed since considered as out-of-scope. These bugs were found using a differential fuzzing approach and [gosentry](https://github.com/kevin-valerio/gosentry).

topPRs.title: test(contracts): stage past NUT bundles in L2 fork upgrades
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Stages committed prior NUT bundles during live L2 fork upgrade test setup so fork tests can run on chains that have not yet applied earlier NUT-backed forks.

Failure shape this fixes:

```
ExecuteNUTBundle: Transaction failed - Deploy StorageSetter Implementation - Proxy: implementation not initialized
```

That happens when the current bundle expects Karst-era `ConditionalDeployer` / L2CM infrastructure that is not present on the forked chain.

This adds:
- Ordered NUT bundle discovery from `op-core/nuts/fork_lock.toml` via a new `scripts/go-ffi/go-ffi nut-bundles` command.
- Reusable `ExecuteNUTBundle.executePath(string)` and `ExecuteNUTBundle.executeAll(NetworkUpgradeTxn[])` APIs; `execute()` is preserved as a thin wrapper around the current bundle path.
- Test-only `PastNUTBundles` library that fetches ordered prior bundles, extracts each bundle's L2CM from the final `IL2ProxyAdmin.upgradePredeploys` call, and stages or skips each bundle via a centralized skip policy.
- `foundry.toml` read permission for `../../op-core/nuts/`.
- Wiring into `L2ForkUpgrade_TestInit.setUp()` only, after `generateScript.run()` and before common state capture.

**Skip policy**

Same-L2CM skipping alone is too broad: Karst and a future Interop bundle can share the same final L2CM, so a naive same-L2CM skip drops Karst even when the forked chain has never applied it. `_shouldSkipPriorBundle` applies these rules in order:
- Karst direct CREATE2 bootstrap supersession: skip when the current bundle already contains a byte-identical `(to, data)` transaction whose `to == Preinstalls.DeterministicDeploymentProxy`. These direct CREATE2 calls are not idempotent; staging Karst first would cause a CREATE2 collision in the current bundle.
- Karst state-aware staging: when Karst's L2CM matches the current bundle, still stage Karst if the live fork's `ConditionalDeployer` is uninitialized.
- Generic same-L2CM skip for non-Karst bundles.

This is intentionally a named-rules list, not residual per-transaction de-dup. Executing only a prior bundle's "unique tail" can violate bundle ordering and prerequisites.

**Non-goals**

- No production activation changes.
- No genesis fork staging — `L2GenesisForkUpgrade.t.sol` is intentionally untouched.
- No Interop wrapper replay (`setFeature(INTEROP)`, `ETHLiquidity` funding, optional `CrossL2Inbox` deploy/upgrade). The FFI is fork-name-aware so wrapper dispatch can be added later without redesigning discovery.

**Tests**

Added coverage for:
- Ordered NUT bundle FFI behavior, lock parsing, path resolution, error cases.
- `ExecuteNUTBundle.executePath` / `executeAll` happy path and revert-message preservation.
- L2CM extraction and rejection of malformed final txs (wrong target / wrong selector / wrong calldata length / non-zero high padding / zero address / empty bundle).
- Same-L2CM skip, Karst direct CREATE2 bootstrap skip, Karst same-L2CM staging when `ConditionalDeployer` is not initialized, and non-overlapping different-L2CM execution.

**Forward-compat check**

Verified against a PR #20397-shaped branch (Karst + Interop lock entries, current bundle is Interop-shaped, both committed bundles decode to the same final L2CM):

```
PastNUTBundles: 2 prior bundle entry/entries discovered
PastNUTBundles: staging fork=karst ...
PastNUTBundles: skipping fork=interop ... (L2CM matches current)
```

Full `test/L2/fork/L2ForkUpgrade.t.sol` passed on that branch. This validates ordered discovery, Karst prerequisite staging, and same-L2CM Interop skip. It does not validate Interop wrapper replay, which remains out of scope.

**Metadata**

- Fixes #20524

topPRs.title: fix(op-supernode): stabilize superroot_atTimestamp Data field
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Closes #18667.

Reworks `superroot_atTimestamp` so the `Data` field is stable for a given timestamp and consistent with `CurrentL1`:

- **Stability** — verified-branch `Data` is sourced from verifiedDB-pinned `(chainID, blockHash)` plus EL-by-hash reads, so subsequent calls for the same T return byte-identical `SuperRoot` and `VerifiedRequiredL1` regardless of EL churn.
- **Regime split** — pre-activation falls back to optimistic outputs (always canonical pre-interop); `T ∈ [activation, firstVerifiable)` falls back to optimistic outputs as well, since the safe-head startup handoff covers ts; `T ≥ firstVerifiable` either returns the verified entry or `Data=nil` with `CurrentL1` communicating verifier progress.
- **Race fix** — `VerifiedResultReader.VerifiedResultAtTimestamp` now returns the verifier's `CurrentL1` captured atomically with the verifiedDB read. The handler reports `min(aggregate.CurrentL1, snapshotL1)` so the response's \`CurrentL1\` cannot overstate verifier progress relative to the verifiedDB observation, closing the window where a rewind or commit between the two reads produced a \`{CurrentL1: high, Data: nil}\` answer that callers would interpret as final.
- **Mid-rewind Data is returned, not errored** — when an entry exists but \`CurrentL1\` has fallen below its \`VerifiedRequiredL1\` (verifier rolled back, entry not yet deleted) the call returns the entry rather than erroring. Callers gate trust on \`CurrentL1 >= VerifiedRequiredL1\` themselves, so returning the preview is more useful than refusing.
- **Pre-Start nil-ctx guard** — Supernode registers each activity's RPC API before scheduling its Start goroutine, so a `superroot_atTimestamp` call can reach the interop reader before `i.ctx` is populated. Added an `ErrNotStarted` sentinel routed to the same optimistic-composition fallback used for `ErrNotActive` / `ErrBeforeVerifiedDB`, so callers get a valid response and can retry once startup completes.

A follow-up bug surfaced during review (optimistic-branch \`RequiredL1\` pairs the original pre-replacement output with the replacement block's L1) is filed separately as #20657; it requires a deny-list schema change and is out of scope here. (Edit: this turned out to not be a bug)

topPRs.title: feat(op-supernode,op-interop-filter): raft-wal-backed LogsDB
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Replaces the op-supervisor `logs.DB` used by op-supernode and op-interop-filter with a new raft-wal-backed implementation that is fully atomic on every `SealBlock`.

Each sealed block is one raft-wal entry: a fixed-width 80-byte header (block hash, parent hash, timestamp, log count, execMsg count), then `logCount × 32`-byte log hashes, then `execMsgCount × 88`-byte executing-message records. `Contains` is therefore an O(1) memcpy into the hash array regardless of how many logs the block carries. `AddLog` buffers in memory; the next `SealBlock` writes the full entry in a single fsync'd raft-wal append.

`op-supervisor` is not touched — both call sites swap from `logs.NewFromFile` to `raftwallogdb.Open` (directory-rooted instead of a single file).

## Benchmarks against the existing logs.DB

One week of 1-second blocks (604,800 blocks), 8 logs/block, fsync per `SealBlock`:

| Backend | Write time | Per block | Disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| existing logs.DB (no fsync) | ~30 s | ~17 µs | 317 MiB |
| raft-wal + fsync | 7 m 46 s | 770 µs | 384 MiB |

At 197 logs/block (op-mainnet average), measured directly:

| Metric | raft-wal value |
|---|---|
| Write time (week) | 12 m 18 s |
| Per sealed block | 1.22 ms |
| Disk (week) | 3.75 GiB |

Read latency at 2,000 blocks / 8 logs:

| Op | logs.DB | raft-wal |
|---|---|---|
| `Contains` | 46 µs | 3.9 µs |
| `OpenBlock` | 47 µs | 3.0 µs |

The offset-index entry layout means `Contains` does not degrade with logs/block — a block of 2,214 logs still answers `Contains` with a single bounded read + memcpy + checksum.
